result.summary: Fixes two regressions in the bitcoin-cli lightweight HTTP client introduced by the removal of libevent. It treats HTTP responses with Content-Length: 0 as complete instead of waiting for a connection close, and restores -rpcclienttimeout to act as an idle timeout per socket read rather than a fixed overall phase deadline.
result.problem: In bitcoin-cli, responses with Content-Length: 0 (such as RPC authentication errors) fell into the branch for lengthless responses and hung until the server closed the connection. Additionally, -rpcclienttimeout was altered from an inactivity timeout to a strict phase deadline, causing large or slow RPC responses to be aborted even while incoming data was actively arriving.
evidence: Post-merge review by b-l-u-e on #34342 pointed out the Content-Length handling flaw: 'b-l-u-e found this in post-merge review in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34342#discussion_r3358700705'
PR description highlights that without resetting on data arrival, '-rpcclienttimeout no longer measures real idle time... so a large/slow response could be cut off while data still arrives.'
result.scope_notes: Follow-up fixes to merged PR #34342 ('cli: Replace libevent usage with simple http client'). The author noted that the timeout fix does not include automated tests due to flakiness.
result.card: Fixes two regressions in the bitcoin-cli custom HTTP client introduced when libevent was removed in #34342. HTTP responses with Content-Length: 0 are now recognized as complete immediately rather than reading until socket disconnection. In addition, -rpcclienttimeout is restored to an idle timeout that resets on data arrival, preventing large or slow responses from being terminated prematurely while active data transfer is ongoing. These address an issue flagged in post-merge review of #34342.

risk.why: A flaw in bitcoin-cli's HTTP client could cause CLI commands to hang or terminate with spurious timeout errors.
